prior_importants.description: The non-regular-file refusal only runs for a path `isSkillManifest` matches, but `.claude/skills/**/*.md` also lifts `.claude/skills/shadow.md`. Committed as a symlink to a directory (e.g. `../../docs/shadow`, holding a `SKILL.md` with `name: pr-ci-review`), that path is never read and its mode is never checked, so the scope audit passes it.

The new name check fails open because `FRONTMATTER`/`FRONTMATTER_OPENING` are narrower than Claude Code's frontmatter parser at both delimiters. (A) An opening `---` followed by NBSP, `\f` or `\v` before the LF matches neither regex, so `isMisnamedSkill` returns false. (B) A `---` in the middle of a line, as in `name: pr-ci-review---`, does not close the block for the gate, but a lazy reader closes there.

The gate closes frontmatter only at a `---` that starts a line, so `.claude/skills/pr-ci-review---/SKILL.md` with `name: pr-ci-review---` passes: its name equals its directory. A reader that closes at the first `---` anywhere reads `name: pr-ci-review` and registers `/pr-ci-review`.

PROTECTED_WITHIN_EXCEPTIONS keeps only `.claude/skills/pr-ci-review/**` protected, but the CI review allows a bare `"Skill"` permission, so any other worker-merged skill can be loaded by every later CI review with the repo token — the harm ADR 0208 gives as its reason for protecting pr-ci-review.

findings.description:
The strict frontmatter form still allows a lone CR (and NEL/LS/PS) inside the YAML. yaml v2 does not treat a lone CR as a line break, but the YAML 1.2 spec and js-yaml do. So `---
description: x #name: pr-ci-review
---
` in `.claude/skills/zz/SKILL.md` reads as a comment to the gate, which sees no `name:` and passes it. A reader that breaks lines on CR sees `name: pr-ci-review`.
findings.body:
**A lone CR inside the frontmatter lets two readers see different names**

ADR 0208 says the gate accepts one strict form so that no reader can read a shorter or different block than the gate does. `FRONTMATTER` requires a bare LF on the opening line, but it reads each YAML line as `[^\n]*\n`. That lets a lone `\r` (and U+0085/U+2028/U+2029) sit inside the block, and the only extra check is for `---`:

```ts
const FRONTMATTER = /^---\n((?:[^\n]*\n)*?)---(?:\n|$)/;
...
const [, yaml = ''] = block;
if (yaml.includes('---')) return true;
```

**Trigger.** A worker commits `.claude/skills/zz/SKILL.md` containing `---\ndescription: x #\rname: pr-ci-review\n---\n`.

- **The gate.** yaml `^2.9` ends a line only on `\n` and strips only a CR that comes right before an LF. It reads `#\rname: pr-ci-review` as one comment, so `front` is `{ description: 'x' }`. There is no `name`, `isMisnamedSkill` returns `false`, and the file merges.
- **Another reader.** The YAML 1.2 spec (`b-break` includes a bare carriage return) and js-yaml (`is_EOL` covers 0x0D) both break the line at the CR. They read `name: pr-ci-review`, which gives a skill outside the protected directory that answers `/pr-ci-review`.
- **NEL/LS/PS.** These are line breaks only in YAML 1.1. The ADR already models YAML 1.1 for merge keys, so refusing them too is consistent.
- **Block scalar.** `description: |\n  a\rname: pr-ci-review\n` is the same root cause.

Claude Code's frontmatter parser is not in-tree, hence medium confidence. The existing tests cover CR only in the CRLF cases. Refusing these characters affects none of the 29 skills in the repo, since none contains a CR.

<https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/496289b02a35010be37f5d5120862f5f1ef4b9f5/src/core/skill-name.utils.ts#L13-L33>

findings.description: A nested manifest such as `.claude/skills/a/pr-ci-review/SKILL.md` with no `name:` passes. The gate's own model (ADR: no `name:` means the skill takes its directory's) names it `pr-ci-review`, yet only the declared name is compared to CI_REVIEW_SKILL, and PROTECTED_WITHIN_EXCEPTIONS covers only the top-level directory.
findings.body:
**A nested `pr-ci-review` directory with no `name:` gets past the gate**

`SKILL_MANIFEST` matches a manifest at any depth and takes the leaf directory as the skill's name. When `name:` is absent, `isMisnamedSkill` returns `false`, and the `CI_REVIEW_SKILL` comparison only runs on a declared name:

```ts
const directory = SKILL_MANIFEST.exec(path)?.[1];
if (directory === undefined) return false;
...
if (front === null || typeof front !== 'object' || !('name' in front)) return false;
const { name } = front;
return typeof name !== 'string' || name.toLowerCase() === CI_REVIEW_SKILL || name !== directory;
```

`PROTECTED_WITHIN_EXCEPTIONS` is `` [`.claude/skills/${CI_REVIEW_SKILL}/**`] ``, which compiles to the anchored `^\.claude/skills/pr\-ci\-review/.*$`.

**Trigger.** A worker with scope `.claude/skills/**` commits `.claude/skills/a/pr-ci-review/SKILL.md` containing `---\ndescription: x\n---\n`.

- The path is lifted, and the protected regex cannot match it because of the extra segment.
- The file is plain and in the strict form, and it has no `name`, so the merge passes.
- ADR 0208 says "A skill with no `name:` takes its directory's", and the test "reads the directory a SKILL.md sits in, at any depth" treats nested manifests as skills. By that model this skill is `pr-ci-review`.
- The same file with `name: pr-ci-review` written out is refused, so the gate disagrees with itself.
- A nested `a/PR-CI-REVIEW/` gets through the same way.

Whether Claude Code discovers skills below the top level is not in-tree, hence medium confidence.

**Fix.** Refuse a manifest whose directory is `pr-ci-review` in any case. A legitimate edit to the top-level `.claude/skills/pr-ci-review/SKILL.md` is unaffected, because `isProtected` refuses that path before any content check runs.

<https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/496289b02a35010be37f5d5120862f5f1ef4b9f5/src/core/skill-name.utils.ts#L28-L42>
findings.suggestion:
if (directory === undefined) return false;
  if (directory.toLowerCase() === CI_REVIEW_SKILL) return true;

process_issues.description: The conventions reviewer read docs/conventions/general.md but not testing.md, and did not read the ADR 0208 or test-file diffs, so testing conventions for the delta's test changes went unchecked.
